READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

- file: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f0.sh:19
- category: duplication
- title: Driver-test preamble (build_driver.sh + BIN resolution + -x check) copy-pasted in ~27 contract scripts
- detail: The trio BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"; bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"; [ -x "$BIN" ] || fail ... recurs across the suite: grep counts 28 build_driver.sh call sites (26 files in tests/andes_sim/ plus tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh and tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f0.sh twice) and 30+ BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim" lines including tests/vplat/. tests/lib/log.sh's own header states it exists because 'These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts' - a require_driver() helper there (build + set BIN + assert executable) is the same consolidation move, and every one of these scripts already sources log.sh.
- claimed safety: Extraction of byte-identical lines into a sourced function; the fail messages and >/dev/null 2>&1 redirection are preserved, so per-script behavior and output are unchanged.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.

Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F0 contract: scaffold + build for andesim.
3	#
4	#   1. scripts/build_driver.sh builds build/andesim (executable).
5	#   2. andesim with no args prints usage and exits non-zero.
6	#   3. andesim -h prints usage and exits zero.
7	#
8	# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development
9	# (mirrors tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh). Not wired into run_e2e.sh.
10	set -uo pipefail
11	
12	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
13	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
14	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
15	
16	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
17	
18	# 1. build produces an executable
19	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
20	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
21	
22	# 2. no args -> usage on output, non-zero exit
23	out=$("$BIN" 2>&1); rc=$?
24	[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "no-args exit code should be non-zero, got 0"
25	echo "$out" | grep -qi "usage" || fail "no-args output missing 'usage':"$'\n'"$out"
26	
27	# 3. -h -> usage on output, zero exit
28	out=$("$BIN" -h 2>&1); rc=$?
29	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "-h exit code should be 0, got $rc"
30	echo "$out" | grep -qi "usage" || fail "-h output missing 'usage':"$'\n'"$out"
31	
32	ok "F0 scaffold: build, usage"
33

1	# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
2	#
3	#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
4	#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
5	#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
6	#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
7	#
8	# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
9	# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"
10	
11	fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
12	ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }
13	
14	expect() {
15	  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
16	  local out rc
17	  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
18	  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
19	  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
20	}
21	
22	# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
23	_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
24	
25	# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
26	# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
27	cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }
28	
29	# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
30	# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
31	vsim_bin_dir() {
32	  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
33	  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
34	}
35

2	# `andesim profile` LLM report contract (real QEMU + the hot-loop TCG plugin):
3	# each loop block carries a ready hybrid pc window,
4	# `measure: --pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>`, derived from the loop's
5	# enclosing function (one-shot pc triggers fire on the first hit, so the
6	# function span covers every iteration and needs no objdump step).
7	#
8	# profile is engine-synced, so the test ships a fake cycle-accurate engine
9	# (ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR) whose --describe pins vlen=512 and whose
10	# --print-qemu-config names andes-ax45mpv -- the same cfg staging a real
11	# vsim engine gets, without needing one built. The plugin path is NOT
12	# overridable from the CLI: the run proves the bundled
13	# qemu_plugin/libhotIterationLoop.so resolution end to end.
14	#
15	# Builds a tiny single-ret RVV kernel (vplat runtime), profiles it, and
16	# checks the measure line against the toolchain's own nm/objdump as the
17	# oracle.
18

input.reason: Duplication is real and larger than claimed: the build line `bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"` is byte-identical in 34 files (27 tests/andes_sim + 7 tests/vlinux; claim said 28 sites/26 files and missed vlinux). But the claimed safety ("fail messages preserved, behavior and output unchanged") does not hold for the population as characterized: (1) the `[ -x "$BIN" ]` leg has 6 distinct fail messages ("missing executable", "missing andesim binary", "missing driver binary", "driver not built", "need build/andesim", "need build/andesim + a fixture ELF") plus 2 scripts using it as an if-condition, so a single hardcoded-message helper changes output text in ~20 scripts unless the message is parameterized; (2) tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh does NOT source log.sh (contradicting the claim) and uses a conditional build (only when BIN missing, no fail on build error) with a differently formatted stdout FAIL line - folding it in changes both execution and output; (3) 9 andes_sim scripts (f5-f9, trigger_gating, verify, profile, release_surface) build but have no -x check, so a trio helper adds a new assertion; (4) vplat scripts and test_vlinux_boot.sh have BIN + -x check but deliberately no build call - a build-included helper would make them start building. Safe only if scoped to the 34 identical build lines with a message-parameterized (or omitted) -x check and the plugin/vplat/if-condition sites left alone.
